subject: Re: Arcadia — priority gating for multi-tenant isolation and quantization
messages:
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.ai>
To: Product Eng <dev@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Arcadia — priority gating for multi-tenant isolation and quantization

Team,

Quick heads-up: Arcadia (prospect, 3rd largest PFM in our west-coast pilot cohort) has surfaced two must-haves in procurement that are gating contract signature this quarter. Marissa and Karthik are looping me in to accelerate alignment with Product/Eng. The asks are: 

- Tenant-level isolation for non-production model caching (customer wants separate cache namespaces for dev/staging/prod)
- A supported quantized model profile for our Llama-3-70B variant with validated latency targets (90th pctl <= 220ms at 1 request/sec)

Why this matters: Arcadia is prepared to sign a 3-year Dedicated commitment (estimated ARR $1.2M) if we can show an implementation plan and rough timelines by EOW Friday. Procurement specifically called out the caching isolation as a security/compliance checkbox and wants it in the product roadmap or as an engineering exception with a mitigation plan.

Can Product/Eng weigh in on feasibility and an estimated delivery window? If we can scope a minimal ship (config flag + prefixing + docs) for isolation and a quantization runbook with perf targets, that might be sufficient for their legal/procurement team.

I attached the mutual action plan from Arcadia and a small CSV extract of SLO items they sent.

Primary asks:
1) Feasibility (yes/no) for isolation as a configurable product feature (not full multi-tenant rewrite)
2) Bandwidth estimate (engineering weeks) to implement gating (config + doc + e2e test)
3) Risk/mitigations if we put this as an exception instead of product scope

Marissa/Karthik: please add any customer nuance I missed.

Thanks,
Maya
Maya Srinivasan
Senior Director, Customer Growth — Redwood Inference

Adding color from the Arcadia side:
- Champion: Oliver Grant (Head of AI Platforms) — wants an explicit timeline and interim mitigations.
- Legal/procurement are comfortable with a roadmap entry + an interim engineering exception if we can commit to a delivery window and some contractual language (SLA carve-outs).
- Primary risk for them is accidental cache bleed between stages which would violate their internal compliance for PII-handling pipelines.

Customer ask is not a full, hardened tenant isolation product — they explicitly said they would accept a configuration toggle that prefixes caches per environment and an operational SOP we own.

They've asked us to provide the timeline by Friday so they can move the contract to signature.

Marissa

Subject: Re: Arcadia — priority gating for multi-tenant isolation and quantization

Thanks for the clear summary. Quick technical notes and questions: 

1) Cache isolation
- Implementing per-environment cache prefixes is straightforward from a runtime perspective (config + namespace prefixing) ~ 2–3 engineering weeks (1 engineer + QA) to ship a supported toggle, docs, and E2E.
- Risk: if customers run in shared pools, the prefixing reduces but does not eliminate cross-tenant inference side-channels. For Arcadia's ask (dev/staging/prod namespace isolation within their own tenant), prefixing satisfies the procurement checkbox.

2) Quantized Llama-3-70B profile
- We can produce a quantization profile (4-bit QAT or GPTQ) and validate 90th pctl latency on our Dedicated infra in approx 4 weeks (model conversion + perf runs + small infra tweaks).
- Unknowns: their peak seq-length distribution. Perf target depends on seq-length; need the customer's typical distribution.

Scope recommendation (minimal viable commitment to get contract signed):
- Ship per-environment cache prefixing as a configurable flag (2–3w) + docs + canary rollout to a dedicated pool.
- Deliver a quantization runbook and a trial perf report for a representative sample within 4w; we can include that in an appendix to the roadmap entry.

If Sales wants firm dates, we should allocate an engineer for the week of 5/31 to start the cache work and schedule model perf runs the week after.

Dev
Dev Patel
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference

From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@arcadia.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sasha Bloom <sasha.bloom@arcadia.ai>, procurement@arcadia.ai
Date: Tue, 24 May 2027 08:16:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Arcadia — priority gating for multi-tenant isolation and quantization

Thanks, Maya/Marissa — appreciate the quick coordination. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- Seq length: our pipelines average 512 tokens, spikes up to ~1,800 for reports; if that changes your perf estimates please flag.
- For procurement: a roadmap entry that says "Configurable environment cache prefixing (ETA: 3 weeks)" + an engineering exception with mitigation steps (audit logs + canary test plan) would be acceptable to legal for signature.
- For quantization: we don't need production-grade latency for all workloads day 1. A validated trial on Dedicated capacity with defined perf numbers is OK.

If you can return dates by Friday we can proceed to legal and finalize the commercial terms.

Oliver
Oliver Grant
Head of AI Platforms, Arcadia.ai

Actionable plan (agreed):

- Quantization trial: schedule model conversion and perf testing for Llama-3-70B. Estimated effort: 1 engineer + infra runs over 3 weeks. Target start: 2027-06-07. Trial report available by 2027-06-28.
- Interim mitigations for signature: provide contractual language stating these items are "roadmap entries with committed delivery windows" and attach the engineering exception (audit logs + canary plan).

Please confirm and I'll add the roadmap ticket and link to the mutual action plan in HubSpot.

Thanks,
